text: . Union Culture and Tourism Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat will inaugurate the 68th All India Kalidas Samaroh in Ujjain today. Chief Minister Dr Mohan Yadav will also be present at the event. The seven-day festival will begin at 6 PM at the Pt. Suryanarayan Vyas Sankul Hall of the Kalidas Sanskrit Academy. On this occasion, well-known theatre artist Vani Tripathi Tikoo will receive the National Kalidas Award 2026 in the field of theatre. She is being honoured for her outstanding contribution to theatre and her long dedication to the art.The award includes a tax-free cash prize of Rs. 5 lakh, a citation plaque, a shawl and a coconut. Since 1982, a total of 37 eminent personalities have received this award. The festival will feature cultural performances by renowned artists from across the country. It is being organised jointly by the Culture Department, Kalidas Sanskrit Academy and Samrat Vikramaditya University. The festival will continue until November 27. An All India Dance-Drama Competition will also be held on November 26. The winning team will receive Rs. 5 lakh, the second-place team will get Rs. 3 lakh, and the third-place team will be awarded Rs. 1 lakh.

. The 45th Indian International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 will begin tomorrow at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. Talking to media, Chairman of India Trade Promotion Organisation, Jawed Ashraf said that this year the focus is on three key aspects that are enhancing the visitor experience, showcasing innovations and highlighting India’s rich heritage. He said that visitors can book tickets online through the IITF 2026 mobile application, which is integrated with the DMRC’s Sarthi app. Mr Ashraf informed that shuttle bus services will operate from several metro stations, including Mandi House, connecting visitors to all entry gates of the venue. Visitors can also reach Bharat Mandapam through app-based taxis, private vehicles and public transport. He added that parking facilities for around three thousand vehicles have been arranged, along with designated waiting areas for app-based taxis. Special facilities, including wheelchair assistance will also be available for senior citizens to ensure a comfortable and convenient experience.

. Presidents of the US, China and Russia concluded their unprecedented trilateral meeting yesterday by issuing a Declaration Towards Peace, calling for UN reforms and outlining plans to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products to ease the energy crisis. The three Presidents Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin – in their four-point declaration also agreed to hold dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons.They also agreed that the International Criminal Court and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction. Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin met for the three-way summit on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit at the Kylin Villa in Shenzhen. Trump had expressed his intention to discuss nuclear arms reductions and other major international issues at the three-way summit.

. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare’s dedicated Health Pavilion at the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 in New Delhi is showcasing its flagship health programmes and public healthcare initiatives. The theme of this year’s Health Pavilion is Yuva Bharat, Swasth Bharat, highlights preventive healthcare, healthy lifestyles and youth participation in building a healthier nation. The Pavilion was inaugurated by NITI Aayog Member, Dr M Srinivas, in the presence of Health Secretary, Punya Salila Srivastava.Addressing the gathering, Dr. Srinivas emphasised on preventive healthcare and healthy lifestyle choices to address rising burden of Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs) and lifestyle-related health conditions. He also highlighted the importance of public awareness, early detection and timely medical intervention in preventing and managing NCDs. Outlining the benefits of Health Pavilion, Dr. Srinivas said that it offers a valuable opportunity for citizens to learn about common health risks, understand preventive measures and familiarise themselves with various Government healthcare programmes and services. He also encouraged visitors to actively participate in the Pavilion’s activities and use the opportunity to enhance their understanding of health and well-being.The Ministry noted that in the Pavilion 39 stalls representing 24 national health programmes and organisations showcase Government’s healthcare initiatives, achievements and services. The Ministry also highlighted that a dedicated TB stall has been established to raise awareness about tuberculosis and TB screening is being conducted using AI-enabled handheld X-ray technology. The Pavilion also included interactive activities, live cpr demonstrations, health awareness sessions and dedicated kids’ zone to engage visitors and promote healthy living. The Ministry said that the Pavilion provides an important platform to connect directly with citizens, showcase the Government’s wide-ranging healthcare initiatives and promote greater public awareness about preventive healthcare, early diagnosis and healthier lifestyles.

. Japanese film Look Back, directed by Hirokazu Koreeda, premiered today in the Cinema of the World section at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), receiving a warm response from audiences.The critically acclaimed film has earned international recognition, winning five collateral awards at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival 2026, including the Cinema and Art Award, SIGNIS Award, Cinema Sara Award, UNIMED Award and Fanheart3 Award – Special Mention. It has also been showcased at prestigious international festivals, including the Toronto International Film Festival and Busan International Film Festival.Look Back tells the story of Fujino, an outgoing school student, and Kyomoto, a socially withdrawn girl, who develop a deep friendship through their shared passion for manga creation. The film traces their evolving bond and artistic journeys as they grow into adulthood.The screening at IFFI received a warm welcome, with viewers appreciating its poetic storytelling, emotional depth and cinematic treatment. The direction, performances and striking cinematography by Senzo Ueno were among the highlights that resonated with audiences.The 57th IFFI is being organised in Goa from November 20 to 28 under the theme “Stories Without Borders”, showcasing acclaimed films and cinematic voices from across the world.

. The Indian women’s hockey team defeated Malaysia 4-1 in the Women’s Asian Hockey Champions Trophy being held in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh. Khan Mumtaz, captain Salima Tete, Pooja Sahu and Lalremsiami scored one goal each for India. Nuramirah Zulkifli scored the only goal for Malaysia.Earlier in the day, China defeated Thailand 7-0 in the opening match. Feng Qiagmiao and Deng Qiuchan scored two goals each for China, while three other players scored one goal each.In the second match of the day, Japan defeated South Korea 1-0. The match remained goalless until the final minutes. In the 59th minute, Saito Hanami scored from a penalty corner to give Japan the win.Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav inaugurated the tournament today. The stadium was lit up with a grand fireworks display, and a large number of spectators came to watch the matches. Six countries, including India, are taking part in the tournament.The tournament is being held at the International Sports Complex in Barkheda Nathu, Bhopal, from November 19 to 28. Entry to the stadium is free for spectators.On Saturday, China will play Malaysia at 2:30 PM, Thailand will face Japan at 4:45 PM, and hosts India will take on South Korea at 7 PM.

. The combined Index of Core Industries (ICI) registered growth of 10.9 per cent in October on an annual basis driven by strong performance in iron ore, coal, electricity and cement sectors. This is higher than the upwardly revised growth rate of 8.2 per cent recorded in September. According to the provisional estimates released by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry today, six out of nine core sectors recorded positive growth last month. Among these, iron ore production recorded the highest growth at 26.4 per cent. Coal production accelerated by 23.1 per cent, electricity generation increased by 21.6 per cent, cement production gained 15.4 per cent, steel production output grew by 7.3 per cent, and refinery products expanded by 3.4 per cent on an annual basis. However, natural gas production fell by 7.6 per cent, crude oil production dipped by 4.1 per cent, and fertilizer production declined by 12.2 per cent in October on an annual basis.

. India today scored 486 for 4 at stumps on Day 3 of the opening Test against hosts New Zealand at the Basin Reserve in Wellington. The Visitors finished the day with a significant 118-run first-innings lead over the hosts, who were dismissed for 368.KL Rahul slammed a historic century, producing a magnificent 136 off 290 deliveries, with the help of nine fours and two sixes. Rahul also became the first Indian opening batter to score Test centuries in all four SENA countries, South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia.  Rahul received excellent support from Devdutt Padikkal, who scored a valuable 80 runs. The duo stitched together a brilliant century partnership to strengthen India’s position.Earlier, India won the toss and elected to bowl. The Indian pace attack, led by Jasprit Bumrah, reduced New Zealand to 70 for five. However, a remarkable sixth-wicket partnership helped the hosts stage a recovery. Henry Nicholls remained unbeaten on 140 off 282 deliveries, while Glenn Phillips scored 118 off 216 balls to guide New Zealand to a strong total. The two-match Test series is the final leg of India’s tour of New Zealand, with crucial ICC World Test Championship points at stake.

. The nationwide ‘Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvad: Know Your Vote’ campaign has concluded with 536 Yuva Samvads conducted across 31 States and Union Territories. The campaign organised by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports through Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat) reached over one lakh young people and involved more than 5000 Youth Icons. The campaign brought discussions on electoral awareness to colleges and educational institutions across the country. It encouraged young people, particularly first-time voters, to understand their voting rights and electoral procedures and participate responsibly in democracy.The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports said that the campaign witnessed participation by Governors, Union Ministers, State Ministers, Members of Parliament and other public representatives. It added that sports personalities and youth icons from the sporting community also participated in programmes, sharing their experiences and encouraging youth participation in sports.The Yuva Samvads provided young participants with opportunities to seek clarity on electoral procedures, discuss voting rights and civic responsibilities, and interact directly with public representatives and Youth Icons.

. The Maintenance Command of the Indian Air Force will organise a two-day ‘Air Festival’ at Vayusena Nagar in Nagpur on November 21 and 22.The festival will feature spectacular performances by the Surya Kiran Aerobatic Team, Sarang Helicopter Display Team and Akash Ganga Skydiving Team. Other major attractions will include demonstrations by the Garud Special Forces and the Air Warrior Drill Team, along with a display of Sukhoi-30 MKI fighter aircraft. Union Minister Nitin Gadkari will attend the event as the chief guest on November 22.The festival aims to inspire the younger generation and familiarise them with the capabilities and operational role of the Indian Air Force. Schools, colleges, NCC cadets and various civil organisations have been invited to participate.Around 5,000 spectators are expected to attend the festival over the two days. However, in view of security considerations, entry will be restricted to invitees only.

. Houthi rebels have claimed responsibility for a drone attack on a tower in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, causing material damage but no casualties. Saudi Arabia’s Directorate General of Civil Defence said the attack damaged a building in the King Abdullah Financial District. Media reports said the strike shattered windows across seven to eight floors of the Public Investment Fund Tower and damaged parts of its exterior facade.The tower houses the headquarters of Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund. Meanwhile, the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted and destroyed several Houthi drones in the southern region of the country. Civil Defence also issued danger alerts for several areas, including Najran, Riyadh, Al Kharj, Jizan, Abha and Khamis Mushait. Houthi-affiliated Al Masirah TV reported that the group claimed four military operations targeting strategic sites in Saudi Arabia.Its spokesperson said the first operation targeted Riyadh’s financial district early Thursday, followed by another strike in the evening. The Houthis claimed that the attacks scored direct hits and caused significant damage.

. World Fisheries Day is being observed today. The day aims to highlight the importance of sustainable fisheries and aquaculture in ensuring food and nutritional security, generating livelihoods and maintaining ecological balance. The observance traces its origins to 1997, when representatives from 18 countries gathered in New Delhi to establish the World Fisheries Forum. The initiative aimed to promote responsible fishing practices and safeguard the rights and interests of fishing communities.The theme for World Fisheries Day 2026 is “Empowering People for Change: Advancing Decent Work in Fisheries and Aquaculture, Particularly for Youth and Women.” The theme highlights the need to promote decent employment opportunities, empower women and young people, and ensure inclusive and sustainable growth across the fisheries and aquaculture sectors.India is the world’s second-largest fish-producing country, accounting for nearly eight per cent of global fish production. The country has made significant progress in the sector over the past decade. India’s total fish production has more than doubled, rising from 96 lakh tonnes to 195 lakh tonnes last year. The fisheries sector is an important pillar of the Indian economy, supporting the livelihoods of millions of people. A coordinated approach involving all stakeholders is aimed at further strengthening the sector, with a focus on increasing fish production, boosting exports and creating more livelihood opportunities.

. US President Donald Trump has praised India’s low interest rates and strong economic growth. He cited India as an example while criticising the US Federal Reserve for damaging the American economy by keeping interest rates high despite strong economic performance. Mr Trump made the comparison at a news conference in Washington last night after returning from a four-day visit to Asia.Referring to India’s economic growth of around seven per cent, President Trump argued that the US economy, currently growing at around four per cent, could expand by 14 to 20 per cent if the Federal Reserve lowered borrowing costs instead of keeping interest rates high. He also said that the United States should be able to borrow money at lower interest rates than any other country. Mr Trump accused the Federal Reserve of taking a political approach to monetary policy and keeping borrowing costs high despite strong economic indicators.The US President further claimed that a 1 percentage point cut in interest rates could save the country 650 billion dollars in debt payments. He also highlighted rising investments in manufacturing, saying factory activity had expanded for ten consecutive months and investment in new equipment had increased by 21 per cent this year. Mr Trump credited his tariff policies with encouraging companies such as Audi and Toyota to invest in manufacturing in the United States.He also pointed to falling oil and petrol prices as signs of economic improvement. He said future petrol prices could depend, in part, on a possible agreement between the United States and Iran. The US Federal Reserve determines interest rates based on economic conditions, particularly inflation and employment, with the twin objectives of maintaining price stability and supporting maximum employment.

. In Peru, a strong magnitude 6.8 earthquake has hit the central region. The initial reports indicated no deaths or major destruction. The Geophysical Institute of Peru reported that the tremor rattled the capital, Lima, and was centred in the Andean region of Junin at a depth of 129 kilometres. This is reportedly the first time an earthquake of this magnitude has been felt in this area as per reports. Peru sits along the Pacific Ring of Fire, a heavily faulted region where shifting tectonic plates regularly cause earthquakes, NBC News noted. Further details are awaited.

. Major Asian stock market indices edged lower today. Taiwan’s Taiex shed over 6.2 per cent, South Korea’s Kospi slumped 5.2 per cent, Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell almost 5.1 per cent, Singapore’s Strait Times dipped nearly 2.1 per cent, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng dropped 1.9 per cent, and China’s Shanghai Composite dipped 1.2 per cent.On the economic front, Japan’s consumer price index (CPI) rose to 2.3 per cent year-on-year in October, up from 2.1 per cent in September. Consumer prices exceeded the Bank of Japan’s two per cent target for the second straight month. Meanwhile, the core CPI, which strips out prices of food, rose to 2.2 per cent last month on an annual basis, higher than 2.1 per cent in the previous month.In European markets, Germany’s DAX dipped 1.8 per cent, and London’s FTSE 100 dropped half a per cent, when reports last came in.

. In Men’s Cricket, Impressive fifties from openers Yashasvi Jaiswal and KL Rahul helped India reach 159 for one in their first innings at stumps in reply to New Zealand’s first-innings total of 368 in the first Test of the two-match series in Wellington. At stumps, Devdutt Padikkal (16 batting) was giving company to Rahul with India trailing by 209 runs.Earlier, India won the toss and elected to bowl; Jasprit Bumrah and the Indian seamers reduced the hosts to 70/5 before a massive sixth-wicket recovery shifted the momentum. Henry Nicholls anchors the innings unbeaten on 140 runs in 282 balls, having shared a 200-plus stand with Glenn Phillips, who was dismissed for 118 runs in 216 balls.This series marks the final leg of India’s tour of New Zealand, with valuable ICC World Test Championship points on the line. Steered by Shubman Gill, the 16-member squad features KL Rahul as vice-captain, alongside key players like Rishabh Pant, Jasprit Bumrah, and Ravindra Jadeja.

. Government e-Marketplace (GeM), the national public procurement portal, has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Tribal Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industry (TICCI) to strengthen the participation of tribal entrepreneurs and enterprises in government procurement. The MoU signed yesterday aims to connect tribal businesses with public procurement opportunities through targeted outreach and sustained handholding support.The MoU was signed by Additional CEO, GeM, Ajit B. Chavan, and Chairman, TICCI, Sudhakar Dharavath. Speaking about the collaboration, CEO, GeM, Mihir Kumar said that this partnership with TICCI is an important step towards expanding public procurement opportunities for tribal entrepreneurs. Under the MoU, TICCI will identify and mobilise tribal entrepreneurs, facilitate regional and national outreach programmes, provide field-level support and develop a network of trainers and mentors. Both organisations will also work together to develop action plans, monitor progress and incorporate feedback from entrepreneurs to improve participation.

. The Ministry of Coal has received 85 bids for 18 coal blocks under the 16th round and the second attempt of the 15th round of commercial coal mine auctions.The Ministry said a total of 26 coal blocks across eight states were offered for auction. The 16th round attracted 83 bids for 17 coal blocks, while the second attempt of the 15th round received two bids for one coal block. Competition has been intense, with 16 of the 26 blocks attracting multiple bids. The latest round has also brought 20 first-time bidders into the commercial coal mining sector, reflecting growing interest among new investors and companies.The Ministry further said that production from captive and commercial coal mines increased by 10.22 per cent to over 210 million tonnes in 2025-26. It added that coal continues to play a crucial role in strengthening India’s energy security as demand rises with economic growth. Since 2020, a total of 145 coal mines have been auctioned through 15 rounds, bringing 44 new companies into the sector. These mines are expected to generate annual revenue of around 47,500 crore rupees and create approximately 4.9 lakh jobs.The Ministry said the auction framework offers several incentives to investors, including no restrictions on the end use of coal, 100 per cent foreign direct investment through the automatic route and low upfront payments. The bids will now be evaluated by a multidisciplinary Technical Evaluation Committee. Technically qualified bidders will be shortlisted to participate in the electronic auction through the MSTC portal.

. India has administered over one crore human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine doses under the National HPV Vaccination Campaign in less than nine months of its launch, marking a major milestone in cervical cancer prevention. Health and Family Welfare Ministry said that the campaign has achieved nearly 87 percent cumulative coverage against the identified annual target cohort of approximately one crore twenty lakh girls, based on the Registrar General of India 2021 population estimates.Akashvani correspondent reports that according to the Health and Family Welfare Ministry, six states including Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Mizoram, Madhya Pradesh and Bihar have achieved 100 percent coverage of their identified target populations under the campaign. Among other high-performing States, Assam has recorded nearly over 96 percent coverage, followed by Telangana with over 95 percent coverage.Meanwhile, Karnataka and Uttarakhand have also recorded more than 90 percent coverage.  In terms of absolute numbers, Uttar Pradesh leads the country with more than 29 lakh 14-year-old girls vaccinated, followed by Bihar with over 13 lakh and Gujarat with nearly 8 lakh girls vaccinated. Launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in February 2026, the nationwide initiative provides free, safe and voluntary single-dose HPV vaccination to 14-year-old girls at government health facilities. The initiative represents a major advancement in India’s preventive healthcare approach, with a focus on safeguarding the health and well-being of future generations of women.Health and Family Welfare Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda congratulated all the states for this achievement. He said that this remarkable progress reflects the collective commitment of States and Union Territories, healthcare professionals, frontline health workers and parents across the country. Mr Nadda said that through government health facilities and U-WIN vaccinator platform, India is moving closer to a future free from cervical cancer.

. The Indian men’s hockey team began its campaign at the 2026 India-New Zealand Century of Sporting Unity Event with a hard-fought 3-2 victory over the hosts in Auckland, New Zealand today.At the Lloyd Elsmore Hockey Stadium, New Zealand took the lead in the 25th minute through Jonty Elmes, who converted a penalty corner into goal. India responded immediately with Uttam Singh finding the equaliser with a field goal.India stepped up their attacking efforts in the second half, with Shardanand Tiwari scoring a field goal to put the visitors ahead. Captain Sanjay then extended country’s advantage with a penalty-corner conversion, taking the score to 3-1. New Zealand continued to push for a goal and reduced the deficit through Sam Hiha, who scored a field goal.India held on to their advantage in the closing stages to secure a 3-2 win and begin the three-match series on a positive note. India will next face New Zealand on Saturday, followed by the third match on Sunday.

. Ace Indian shuttler Lakshya Sen will take on Denmark’s Anders Antonsen in the men’s singles semifinal of the Hong Kong Open Badminton Tournament today. Sen stormed into the semifinals after defeating former world champion and eighth seed Loh Kean Yew of Singapore 21-17, 10-21, 21-13 in the quarterfinals in Kowloon.Meanwhile, the Indian men’s doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty will face Malaysia’s Tee Kai Wun and Man Wei Chong in their semifinal clash. The Indian duo entered the last four after registering an impressive 21-12, 13-21, 21-16 victory over China’s Hu Ke Yuan and Lin Xiang Yi in the quarterfinals.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will share his thoughts with the people of the country and abroad in the Mann Ki Baat programme on Akashvani on 29th November. It will be the 140th episode of the monthly radio programme.People can submit their ideas and suggestions for the programme through the toll-free number 1800-11-7800. They can also share their input online via the Narendra Modi App or the MyGov Open Forum. Citizens can also give a missed call on 1922 and follow the link received in an SMS to directly give their suggestions to the Prime Minister. Ideas and suggestions for the upcoming episode will be accepted until the 27th of this month.

. In the forex market today, the rupee strengthened by 62 paise to close at a seven-month high of 92 rupees and 67 paise against the US dollar. The rupee extended its rising streak for the fifth consecutive session following uninterrupted inflow of foreign funds and a rally in domestic stock markets.The dollar index, which indicates US dollar’s strength against a basket of six other leading currencies, was trading at 103.85 in intra-day trade.

. Young batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi,, women’s World Cup-winning captain Harmanpreet Kaur, Olympic medallists Lovlina Borgohain and Mirabai Chanu were among nine Indian sporting stars named in the TIME100 Next India list.World champion chess player D Gukesh, women’s 400 meter hurdles national record holder Vithya Ramraj, Asian Games gold-winning archer Kumkum Mohod, women’s hockey team goalkeeper Savita Punia and former tennis star Sania Mirza also figured in the prestigious list.TIME has brought out the list for the first time in India. Sooryavanshi, Chanu and Kumkum were listed in the ‘Innovators’ section, while Borgohain, Gukesh and Vithya were named among the Phenoms. Savita figured among the Leaders, while Sania and Harmanpreet found places among the Advocates.

. Prasar Bharati has launched its first script-pitching initiative, ‘Page se Pitch Tak’ (Prasar Bharati Script Pitching Lab), at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Panaji. The programme was inaugurated at the Black Box, Kala Academy, by Prasar Bharati Chairman Prasoon Joshi.The initiative aims to support new and aspiring Indian screenwriters by helping them develop their stories and scripts. It will provide guidance and opportunities to emerging writers across multiple Indian languages, even if they have no prior connections in the film industry.Speaking at the launch, Joshi stressed the need to bring out authentic and unique stories from different parts of India. In line with IFFI 2026’s theme, ‘Stories Without Borders’, the initiative aims to take Indian stories to wider audiences in India and around the world.

. Ace Indian shuttler Lakshya Sen entered the men’s singles semifinals of the Hong Kong Open Badminton with a three-game win over former world champion Loh Kean Yew of Singapore in Kowloon today. Lakshya, who has already sealed his place in the BWF World Tour Finals, notched up an impressive 21-17, 10-21, 21-13 win over eighth seed Loh in the men’s singles quarterfinals. In another quarterfinal match, Kidambi Srikanth lost to Kunlavut Vitidsarn of Thailand 17-21, 7-21.Earlier, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty marched into the men’s doubles semifinals of the tournament with a three-game win 21-12, 13-21, 21-16 over China’s Hu Ke Yuan and Lin Xiang Yia. However, Rakshitha Ramraj’s dream run in women’s singles came to an end with a 19-21, 16-21 defeat to Thailand’s fifth seed Pornpawee Chochuwong in the quarterfinals.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi today called upon youth to break the barriers of limited thinking and unlock new possibilities. He said this while addressing the platinum jubilee celebrations of IIT Kharagpur. PM said that limiting beliefs not only restrict dreams and talent but also restrict the capabilities of the nation.Referring to a recent World Bank Report, the Prime Minister said that around 50 crore people in India have come out of poverty over the past 12 to 13 years. He described this as the outcome of a mindset that believes in breaking limitations and achieving what was once considered impossible.Mr Modi said that the historic land of IIT Kharagpur, which once symbolised the aspirations for freedom and self-governance, is today witnessing India’s resolve towards self-reliance. He highlighted the contribution of  IIT Kharagpur to nation-building over the decades. He underlined the institute’s key role in shaping India’s innovation landscape and called for rising above self-imposed limits to drive national progress. Mr Modi urged students to move forward with the mindset of Nation First. He said that this approach would create new opportunities for them and also greatly benefit the country.

. In Mizoram, three-day Leitlangpui Music Festival is underway in south Mizoram’s Lunglei town, bringing together established musicians, emerging bands and local entrepreneurs to showcase the state’s musical heritage and promote tourism. Organised by the Ministry of Tourism and Mizoram Tourism department, the festival began yesterday at Lena Stadium at Serkawn under the theme “Music Comes Home to Serkawn”. The festival seeks to connect that legacy with contemporary musicians and emerging talent.Addressing the inaugural ceremony, Tourism Minister Lalnghinglova Hmar said music was an inseparable part of Mizoram’s cultural identity and Serkawn held a special place in the state’s musical history. The minister said that the government aimed to take Mizoram’s music and cultural heritage to national and international audiences while creating opportunities for young artists, entrepreneurs and local communities. The festival features performances by established and emerging Mizo musicians.The second day includes a band competition with 10 finalists from Aizawl, Lunglei, Nagaland and Assam, while winners of the previous two editions, Swordtune and Knot, are also scheduled to perform. The final day will feature performances by several Mizo artists and bands, followed by the minister’s address and a fireworks display.

. Amnesty International has urged Bangladesh authorities to stop arresting and harassing garment workers and trade union leaders demanding higher minimum wages. The human rights organisation has expressed concern over what it described as a crackdown on labour activists.Amnesty has called on the government to respect the right to peaceful assembly and distinguish peaceful protesters from those involved in violence. The appeal follows the detention of Green Bangla Garments Workers Federation President Sultana Begum and General Secretary Md Elias by Detective Branch police on November 17. They were detained after participating in a webinar on minimum-wage protests. They reportedly face allegations of obstructing police duties and vandalising factories.Five other labour activists and union representatives were also arrested earlier this month. They include Mostafa Kamal, Rozina Akter Sumi, Md Ali Azgar, Md Morshed Alam Kawsar and Md Fuadur Rahman Nirjon. Amnesty International has called for an end to the targeting of workers exercising their labour rights.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended over one per cent higher for the second straight session today. The Sensex jumped 898 points to close at 83,920. The Nifty climbed 286 points to settle at 25,801.In the broader market on the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index gained almost 0.7 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index dipped over 0.1 per cent.In the Sensex pack, 20 out of 30 constituent companies logged gains. Among the top performers, Kotak Mahindra Bank as well as HDFC Bank jumped over three per cent, Maruti surged nearly 2.9 per cent, and UltraTech Cement climbed almost 2.8 per cent. In contrast, Titan as well as Tata Steel fell 1.7 per cent, NTPC dropped 1.3 per cent, and Hindustan Unilever shed almost one per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 22 out of 28 sectors edged higher. Among the top gainers, Hospitals jumped 3.6 per cent, Private Banks advanced nearly 2.7 per cent and Top 10 Banks added almost two and a half per cent. In contrast, Telecommunication as well as Consumer Durables dropped 0.6 per cent, Industrials lost half a per cent, and Capital Goods dipped nearly half per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was negative, as shares of 2,575 companies declined, 1,804 advanced and 243 remained unchanged.

. In Men’s Cricket, an unbeaten 173-run stand between Henry Nicholls and Glenn Phillips took host New Zealand to 243 at the loss of 5 wickets at stumps on Day 1 of the first Test against India at the Basin Reserve in Wellington today.Nicholls, who slammed his 12th Test century, finished unbeaten on 113, while Phillips will resume his innings on 94 on Day 2. For India, Jasprit Bumrah scalped 3 wickets, while Anshul Kamboj and Akash Deep took one wicket each.Earlier, India won the toss and opted to bowl.

. India’s capital markets have mobilised nearly 9 lakh crore rupees in the first seven months of the current financial year, while market capitalisation has crossed the 5 trillion-dollar mark. Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey has announced further regulatory reforms to attract foreign investment and simplify access to the country’s capital markets.Addressing the CII-DFS Financing Summit 2026 in Mumbai today, Mr Pandey said companies have raised an average of around 10 lakh crore rupees annually through equity and debt instruments over the past decade. He attributed the expansion to strong economic growth, rising investor participation and sustained regulatory reforms. More than 15 crore unique investors are now participating in the securities market.Highlighting the buoyancy in the primary market, the SEBI Chairman said 235 companies have raised around 1.5 lakh crore rupees through Initial Public Offerings so far in the current financial year.He said the corporate bond market is also emerging as an important source of business financing. Outstanding corporate bonds stood at around 62 lakh crore rupees in August this year, equivalent to nearly 55 per cent of bank credit extended to the industry and services sectors. Companies have raised more than 5 lakh crore rupees through bond issuances in FY 2026-27 so far.Mr Pandey also highlighted the growing contribution of Alternative Investment Funds in financing emerging businesses. Their cumulative investments reached around 7.5 lakh crore rupees by September, while committed capital exceeded 18 lakh crore rupees. Assets managed by Real Estate Investment Trusts and Infrastructure Investment Trusts have also crossed 10 lakh crore rupees, supporting infrastructure financing and capital recycling.On regulatory reforms, Mr Pandey said SEBI will soon release a consultation paper proposing further simplification of operations for Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs), including the removal of certain compliance requirements that are not prevalent in other major markets.He said the regulator is working to reduce the FPI onboarding period to as little as five business days. Around 740 FPIs have registered under the Swagat framework, accounting for 17 per cent of total FPI assets under custody.As part of the simplification measures, SEBI has digitised onboarding, permitted digitally signed powers of attorney and enabled net settlement to reduce funding costs. From 1st December, KYC review cycles for applicable FPIs will be extended from one and three years to two and eight years, respectively. Eligible NRIs, overseas citizens of India and foreign nationals can also complete their KYC and re-KYC digitally without travelling to India.Outlining future priorities, Mr Pandey said SEBI is reviewing ICDR and LODR frameworks to eliminate duplicate corporate filings and introduce a single-fine mechanism. It is also working with the RBI and Finance Ministry on a corporate bond market-making framework, reducing REIT and InvIT listing timelines to three working days, and expanding AI-based regulatory tools.On investor safety, he highlighted 45-minute disaster-recovery mandates, SEBI Check, validated UPI handles, and the nationwide ‘Samajh Se Investing Simple’ awareness campaign.

. Prime Minister of Nepal Balendra Shah will pay a two-day State visit to India starting Sunday(Nov 22). This will be his first visit to India after assuming office in March this year. During the visit, the Prime Minister of Nepal will call on President Droupadi Murmu.Prime Minister Narendra Modi will hold bilateral talks with his Nepalese counterpart on Monday(Nov 23) to review the full range of India-Nepal relations and exchange views on regional and international issues of mutual interest. Ministry of External Affairs said India and Nepal share close and friendly relations, rooted in historical, cultural and civilisational links and strong people-to-people ties.Bilateral cooperation has witnessed progress across diverse sectors, including trade and commerce, development partnership, energy and water resources, and physical and digital connectivity, with growing engagement in newer areas such as start-ups, technology and innovation, and sports.The Ministry said the visit continues the tradition of regular high-level exchanges between the two countries and reflects the importance India attaches to its relations with Nepal under its ‘Neighbourhood First’ policy. It will provide an opportunity to further strengthen the bilateral partnership and advance mutually beneficial cooperation.

. Global crude oil prices declined today. Brent crude was trading 0.6 per cent down at 91 US dollars and 44 cents per barrel. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 0.2 per cent down at 82 US dollars and 27 cents per barrel, when reports last came in.

. Under the theme ‘Vikas Aur Virasat’ (Development and Heritage), women-led Self-Help Groups (SHGs) from Tripura, along with various wings under the Department of Industries and Commerce, are participating in the international trade fair being held in New Delhi.At the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026, the Tripura Pavilion is showcasing a wide range of products manufactured by the state’s Self-Help Groups, along with an impressive collection of bamboo and cane handicrafts.Tripura Industries and Commerce Minister Santana Chakma visited the state’s stalls and encouraged the women entrepreneurs, appreciating their efforts. She said their contribution is significant in strengthening Tripura’s economy. She further stated that participation in such fairs would help promote products manufactured in Tripura and increase their recognition in the global market.It may be mentioned that Union Minister for Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal inaugurated the fair on November 13. The exhibition will continue until November 27, with participation from representatives of more than 30 states and Union Territories across the country.

. Union Minister of Food Processing Industries Chirag Paswan has urged beverage companies to innovate and offer healthier beverage alternatives using indigenous superfoods like makhana, millets and sattu. Addressing the Indian Beverage Association Conclave 2026 in New Delhi, the Minister called upon leaders in the food processing industry to build globally recognised Indian Quick Service Restaurant brands and achieve self-reliance in bottling and packaging machinery.Stressing on zero compromise with quality, Mr Paswan asked them to strengthen backward linkages with farmers and Farmer Producer Organisations to ensure uniform taste, meet global standards, and minimise post harvest wastage. The Minister further said that the Government is awared about the challenges faced by the beverage sector and aims to address them.

. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman today chaired the ninth Pre-Budget Consultation with  experts and stakeholders from the housing, urbanisation, and culture sectors in connection with the Union Budget 2027-28, in New Delhi. The meeting was also attended by Secretaries of Department of Economic Affairs and Department of Urban Development.Earlier in the day, the Finance Minister chaired the eighth Pre-Budget Consultation with the stakeholders from employment and labour sectors in connection with the upcoming Union Budget. The meeting was attended by Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs, Anuradha Thakur and senior officials from Ministry of Labour and Employment.The Finance Ministry conducts several pre-Budget consultation meetings annually with experts, industry leaders, economists, and state officials. The deliberations seek to ensure the Union budget reflects diverse perspectives and addresses key economic priorities.

. The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare has said that the country has registered significant growth in vegetable seed exports as well as overall seed exports in recent years. Joint Secretary (Seeds) in the Ministry, Ajeet Kumar Sahu, said that the country’s total seed exports, valued at around 2,023 crore rupees in 2024-25, increased to over 3,000 crore rupees in 2025-26, registering a growth of 30 per cent.Mr Sahu was speaking virtually at a conference on the “Role of Vegetable Seed Sector in Making India a Global Seed Hub”, organised by the Federation of Seed Industry of India (FSII) in New Delhi. He also informed that five Centres of Excellence are proposed to be established in the country, focusing on various aspects of the seed sector, including seed treatment and seed health. He urged the seed industry to prepare a Seed Export Promotion Policy based on a cluster approach, which could be finalised after consultations.Former Director General of the Indian Council of Agricultural Research, Dr Trilochan Mohapatra, called upon the industry to step up investment in research and development in the seed sector. He emphasised the need for India to strengthen its domestic breeding capabilities through molecular breeding and genomic selection and develop crop varieties with superior nutritional qualities.Meanwhile, FSII Chairman Ajai Rana welcomed the government’s commitment to adopting global best practices and standards. He said the proposed five Centres of Excellence would strengthen India’s seed export capabilities. Mr Rana noted that India currently accounts for less than two per cent of global seed trade, while the industry has set an ambitious target of increasing its share to 10 per

. The 3rd All India Police Badminton Cluster 2026-27 is currently underway at the Veer Savarkar Sports Complex in Naranpura, Ahmedabad, Gujarat. Hosted by the Gujarat Police, the national-level championship has entered an exciting phase following impressive performances on the second day of the tournament.Today, a total of 328 matches are scheduled to be played across different categories, including 90 matches in badminton and 238 in table tennis. During yesterday’s second-day events, police athletes from various states and Central Armed Police Forces delivered strong performances across knockout and individual rounds. Hosts Gujarat have also put up an impressive show, particularly in the women’s badminton category.The six-day tournament, which concludes on November 24, features over 1,150 police personnel representing 38 teams from 24 states, four Union Territories, and ten Central Armed Police Forces, including the CRPF, BSF, and CISF. Promoting camaraderie and fitness without rank barriers, the event brings together 463 gazetted officers and 699 non-gazetted personnel, including Gujarat DGP Gyanendra Singh Malik.

. Clashes broke out between activists of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) and the banned Awami League in Bera upazila of Pabna district in Bangladesh. According to local media reports, tensions escalated after Awami League supporters took out a sudden protest procession and marched towards Bera Model Police Station, raising slogans.BNP and its student wing, Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal, activists reached the spot and chased the protesters, triggering clashes and counter-chases. The procession was later dispersed. Later, a haystack near the abandoned residence of former Deputy Speaker Shamsul Haque Tuku was set on fire, and the house was reportedly vandalised. Police confirmed the fire but said the identities of those involved in the arson and vandalism were yet to be established.

. Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports, Dr Mansukh Mandaviya, said that schemes like Khelo India Mission, Fit India Movement and Target Olympic Podium Scheme are helping expand grassroots participation, identify sporting talent and create pathways for high-performance sports. Addressing the 16th edition of FICCI’s Global Summit on the Business of Sports TURF-2026 today in New Delhi, the Minister highlighted the transformation of India’s sporting ecosystem over the past 12 years under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.Mr Mandaviya further said that the vision is to transform India from a sporting nation into a global sports ecosystem. He invited international partners, innovators, manufacturers, and sporting institutions to become part of this transformation. The minister also highlighted the government’s focus on strengthening sports infrastructure and manufacturing capabilities. He said the government has approved a sports goods manufacturing scheme with an outlay of nearly two thousand crore rupees to make India a global hub for sports goods manufacturing and innovation.Calling for greater private sector participation, Mr Mandaviya encouraged industry leaders to invest in sports infrastructure, high-performance academies, sports science facilities, technology and athlete management systems. He further highlighted India’s preparations for the Commonwealth Games 2030 and its ambition to host the 2036 Olympic Games. France is the partner country for this year’s summit, with an MoU signed to strengthen India-France cooperation in the sports sector.

. Union Minister of Education Pralhad Joshi interacted with principals and senior management representatives of CBSE-affiliated schools across the UAE. Speaking at the event held at the Indian High School in Dubai on Friday, he highlighted the contribution of Indian schools to education in the UAE. There are 106 CBSE schools serving over 2.32 lakh students in the UAE.Addressing the gathering, the Minister emphasised the vision of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020. He underlined the focus on holistic and skill-oriented education rooted in Indian values, while promoting critical thinking, creativity and innovation. The Minister also highlighted initiatives such as Atal Tinkering Labs, teacher capacity-building and the growing participation of students in Pariksha Pe Charcha.Mr Joshi said the CBSE Regional Office in Dubai plays a critical role in strengthening educational ties between India and the UAE, and added that efforts would be made to strengthen the office at the earliest. This is the first ever international office of CBSE and was established with the objective of providing localised administrative and academic support to CBSE-affiliated schools overseas, ensuring smoother coordination and timely assistance.The decision to establish the Office was announced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi during his visit to the UAE in February 2024 and the Office began operations in July 2024. While the CBSE Regional Office oversees examinations, school assessments and the implementation of NEP 2020 reforms, the Centre of Excellence (CoE) focuses on teacher training, professional development and promoting innovative, skill-oriented teaching practices.Also present at the interaction were India’s Consul General in Dubai Dr. E Vishnu Vardhan Reddy; and senior officials from the Ministry of Education, CBSE, and the Consulate General of India in Dubai.Later in the evening, the Minister also addressed the Indian Community in Dubai and spoke about the Indian diaspora’s contribution to strengthening India-UAE ties. He highlighted India’s educational and economic transformation under Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the growing potential for collaboration between India and the UAE in higher education, research, innovation and skill development.

. Indian Railways has geared up to manage the ongoing festive season rush of Diwali and Chhath Puja, with extensive crowd management preparations underway at several railway stations. Ministry of Railways said that Indian Railways is developing dedicated passenger holding areas, known as Yatri Suvidha Kendras, at major railway stations across the country. This is being done to streamline passenger movement and ease congestion during periods of heavy footfall, including the festive season. The Yatri Suvidha Kendras, or Passenger Holding Areas, are being developed to provide dedicated space for unticketed and waiting passengers. Our correspondent reports that the facilities have been designed to ensure orderly passenger movement and provide a comfortable waiting environment.The holding areas have been designed to accommodate passengers before they proceed to the platform area. Talking to Akashvani News, Northern Railway CPRO  said that at New Delhi Railway station, a holding area is available for both reserved and unreserved classes. He said additional RPF personnel have also been deployed at Railway stations to facilitate passengers.At Anand Vihar Terminal, the Yatri Suvidha Kendra has 14 ticket counters, 16 CCTV cameras, four electronic display boards and seating for 20 passengers. The facility also has separate toilet facilities for male and female passengers, a Divyangjan toilet, an RO plant, 11 HVLS fans and a public announcement system. The aim is to reduce congestion on platforms, in circulating areas and at station approaches by providing designated spaces for waiting and ticketing.

. Three major works of India’s literary and intellectual heritage including Kalhana’s Rajatarangini, the Mahabharata and Kautilya’s Arthashastra have been included in UNESCO’s Memory of the World Regional Register for Asia and the Pacific. The decision was taken at the 11th session of the register held in Jakarta, Indonesia. With this recognition, India’s total number of inscriptions in the regional register has risen to six. The three works represent different aspects of India’s knowledge traditions. Rajatarangini is a historical account of Kashmir, the Mahabharata explores Dharma, duty and human values, while Arthashastra deals with governance, diplomacy and statecraft. This recognition is a matter of pride for India’s civilisational continuity, its rich knowledge traditions and its contribution to the world. The development was announced by Member Secretary, Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA),  Dr. Sachchidanand Joshi which played an important role in preparing the nomination dossiers for all three works.

. In the Indian bullion market today, 24 carat gold plunged nearly 4.4 per cent to 1,23,893 rupees per 10 grams. Meanwhile, silver also tumbled over 4.9 per cent to 1,52,528 rupees per kilogram according to the closing rates of India Bullion and Jewellers Association.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands tomorrow.The Met Department has also predicted thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Kerala, Mahe and Lakshadweep during the next two days. Similar conditions are expected over Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, and Tripura tomorrow.Meanwhile, the weather agency has forecast mist and shallow fog at most places of Delhi during the morning hours tomorrow.The air quality in Delhi-NCR is in the ‘ Very Poor’ category. According to the Central Pollution Control Board, Delhi’s Air Quality Index was recorded at 303 as of 7 PM today.

. In Bangladesh, at least 50 garment factories remained closed in the Savar and Ashulia industrial belt today as workers continued work abstentions, demanding higher minimum wages, according to local media reports. Industrial Police-1 Superintendent said 11 factories were closed under Section 13(1) of the Bangladesh Labour Act, while others declared holidays following workers’ protests.The industrial belt remained relatively calm, with no reports of major violence or untoward incidents during the morning.Most workers joined production activities peacefully. However, employees at a Ha-Meem Group factory in Ashulia’s Narsinghapur area staged a work abstention, protesting a change in working hours.Workers punched their attendance cards but refused to join production, prompting management to declare a general holiday for the day. Normal operations are scheduled to resume on Sunday. Several other factories also suspended operations following workers’ protests over wage demands. The developments come amid continuing labour unrest in Bangladesh’s ready-made garment sector.

. India and France have unequivocally condemned terrorism in all its forms and manifestations, including cross-border terrorism and violent extremism. The two countries also reiterated their strong condemnation of the terrorist attack in Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir, in April last year, and the terror incident near the Red Fort in New Delhi in November 2025. These issues were discussed at the 18th meeting of the India-France Joint Working Group on Counter-Terrorism, held in New Delhi.The meeting was co-chaired by Additional Secretary (Counter-Terrorism) in the Ministry of External Affairs, Dr Suhel Ajaz Khan, and French Ambassador-at-Large and Special Envoy for Counter-Terrorism and Organised Crime, Olivier Caron.Akashvani correspondent reports that during the meeting, both sides exchanged views on the prevailing terrorist threats in their respective regions and across the world. Discussions also covered state-sponsored terrorism and cross-border terrorism. The two countries reviewed traditional and emerging challenges in combating terrorism. They discussed the threats arising from the misuse of new and emerging technologies, including financial technologies, by terrorists and terrorist groups.The Indian side also briefed the French delegation on India’s comprehensive National Counter-Terrorism Policy and Strategy (PRAHAAR). Both sides discussed ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation in combating the financing of terrorism and online radicalisation. They also explored greater cooperation in information sharing, capacity building, training and the exchange of experiences and best practices. India and France reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation in multilateral forums, including the United Nations, the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) and the No Money for Terror (NMFT) initiative.

. Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSME) Jitan Ram Manjhi today inaugurated the MSME Pavilion at the 45th India International Trade Fair 2026 in New Delhi. On the occasion, Mr Manjhi interacted with artisans and exhibitors at various stalls. He highlighted the importance of khadi as a symbol of country’s rich cultural heritage and traditional craftsmanship. The Minister said that khadi represents country’s traditional industry, entrepreneurship and art. Mr Manjhi also highlighted the PM Vishwakarma Yojana, which covers 18 traditional trades, including barbers, leather artisans, cobblers, garland makers and net weavers.

. Britain and the European Union say they have agreed deals on trade, carbon emissions and youth movement, and pledged to rebuild ties with an ambitious and dynamic post-Brexit relationship. In a joint statement after a summit in Brussels, the UK and EU confirmed agreements that will scrap checks on the trade in plant and animal products, link their emissions trading schemes and let 100,000 young adults from each side live and work in the others’ countries for up to three years.Other areas remain a work in progress, with the two sides giving themselves six months to reach an agreement on the level of student fees for EU students in the UK and vice versa. Today’s summit is part of efforts to forge a closer relationship, a decade after Britain voted to leave the EU and six years after the divorce became final.

. Union Minister of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Shivraj Singh Chouhan has highlighted the importance of healthy livestock in the prosperity of farmers in the country. In an article for a daily newspaper, Mr Chouhan said that keeping animals and birds safe from infectious diseases is not just a veterinary issue but a responsibility to protect the livelihood of farmers and the national economy.He said that animal husbandry, dairy and poultry play a vital role in the agricultural economy; hence, prevention of animal diseases and availability of effective vaccines are integral to the country’s agricultural development strategy. The Minister highlighted that India has made significant progress in indigenous vaccine development against animal and poultry diseases over the past decade. Mr Chouhan emphasised that Indian scientists are now capable of developing innovative solutions to animal diseases according to the needs of the country.The Minister further said that India’s goal is not only to protect its livestock and poultry but also to become a leading global supplier of affordable, effective and quality animal vaccines. Mr Chouhan added that healthy livestock, a secure poultry sector and prosperous farmers are important pillars in India’s journey of Viksit Bharat.
